title: TaxGPT vs Filed: Beyond Automated Tax Prep
summary: TaxGPT vs Filed: compare AI tax preparation, return review, research citations, multi-state coverage, and tax planning to find your platform.
body_markdown:
## Tax Prep: Where They Differ


Both platforms draft returns inside the firm's existing tax software. Filed extracts figures from source documents and enters them into Drake, UltraTax, CCH Axcess, ProConnect, and Lacerte. TaxGPT's[Tax Prep Agent](https://www.taxgpt.com/ai-tax-preparation) operates the same category of software, then completed returns can also be reviewed by Agent Andrew for a first-pass review before they reach the reviewer's desk. The two differ in operating model as much as in scope: Filed's approach is extract, draft, flag, pulling source documents, populating the return, and surfacing anything uncertain for review. TaxGPT Cowork's agents run more autonomously across a workflow, executing multi-step processes end to end and handing off only at the judgment call.


Where they diverge most is workflow breadth. Filed's automation remains centered on the return lifecycle: preparation, review, workpapers, memory, and the planning that follows. TaxGPT Cowork extends into extensions, amended returns, K-1 extraction and creation, R&D credit studies, bookkeeping through month-end close, entity-structure reviews, and other firm workflows.


For multi-state work, the distinction requires some care: TaxGPT Matrix handles multi-state research, letting you run one question across multiple jurisdictions and get a cited comparison table. Filed says multi-state return preparation is still in active development. Multi-state research and multi-state return preparation solve different problems, so we don't treat them as the same capability.


A firm on TaxGPT is automating the extension in April, the 1040-X in July, and the month-end close that never stopped needing doing.


## Return Review: Agent Andrew vs Filed Review


Filed Reviewer and Agent Andrew overlap, but they emphasize different parts of the review process.


Filed Reviewer is heavily focused on source-to-return verification. It reads W-2s, 1099s, K-1s, and other source documents, checks the figures entered on the return against them, builds reviewer-friendly leadsheets, applies firm-specific review rules, and carries prior-year client context such as carryforwards and elections into the review. It can review a return regardless of whether Filed, your staff, or another system prepared it.


[Agent Andrew](https://www.taxgpt.com/agent-andrew) also reconciles completed returns against source documents, flagging transcription, omission, classification, and mismatch issues. But its scope extends beyond data fidelity. Red flags surface errors and audit-risk issues, while green flags identify potential missed deductions, elections, and other tax-saving opportunities. Cleared flags document findings that have already been resolved or rejected.


So the distinction isn't that one “reviews” and the other doesn't. Both provide automated quality control. Filed Reviewer places particular emphasis on source-document reconciliation, reviewer workflows, and firm-specific review rules; Agent Andrew combines source reconciliation with broader audit-risk and tax-savings analysis.


Neither eliminates professional judgment. The useful comparison is which review layer better matches the way your firm already performs quality control.


## Where the Platforms Diverge Beyond the Return Workflow


### Research


Filed has research capability inside its planning workflow. Tax Planner uses specialist research agents to support its recommendations, and its Tax Planning Assistant lets a preparer ask client-specific questions grounded in that client's return and source documents.


Filed's research capabilities sit primarily inside its planning workflow. TaxGPT Research is a dedicated research product for open-ended federal, state, local, Canadian, and cross-border tax questions. TaxGPT covers U.S. federal, state, local, territorial, Canadian, and cross-border tax questions, while Matrix runs the same question across multiple jurisdictions and returns a cited comparison table.


For firms that regularly research issues before a return or planning engagement exists, that distinction matters.


### Drafting


Filed does support drafting in parts of its workflow: Ask can generate client emails, and Tax Planner produces client-ready planning deliverables. Filed supports client-email drafting and planning deliverables, but it does not offer a dedicated tax-writing product comparable to TaxGPT Writer for research memos, IRS notice responses, engagement letters, opinion letters, and other professional tax communications.


TaxGPT Writer drafts tax research memos, IRS notice responses, engagement and opinion letters, client emails, and other tax-specific communications, with research and client context available in the same platform. So when an IRS notice arrives months after filing, TaxGPT has a dedicated workflow for turning the client's facts and supporting authority into the first draft.


### Client Memory


Both platforms retain context, but they organize it differently. Filed's Firm Memory sits across its products and learns from firm-level corrections and rules. Its client memory also carries forward details such as prior-year carryforwards, elections, owner compensation, rental activity, and other client-specific treatment.


TaxGPT's Client Intelligence is structured more explicitly as a client-and-entity intelligence layer. It connects documents, entity relationships, filing history, prior positions, and preferences, then applies that context across research, writing, review, and other TaxGPT workflows.


The distinction is therefore not “memory versus no memory.” It's how broadly that context is modeled and where it can be reused.


### Canada Support


TaxGPT supports Canadian tax research, including the Income Tax Act, CRA guidance, provincial and territorial tax law, GST/HST, and U.S.–Canada treaty questions.


Filed’s publicly listed tax-preparation coverage focuses on U.S. tax forms and does not list Canadian tax-law coverage. TaxGPT supports Canadian federal, provincial, and territorial tax research, including CRA guidance, GST/HST, and U.S.–Canada treaty questions.


## Which Should Your Firm Choose?


Choose Filed if your main bottleneck is the return lifecycle: source-document processing, tax preparation, document-level review, workpapers, prior-year context, and planning from the completed return. If your practice includes significant 1041 or 990 work, Filed currently has broader form coverage in that area. Filed may fit firms whose primary automation needs center on tax preparation, document-level review, workpapers, and planning around the return, particularly when its supported return types and tax-software integrations align with the firm’s existing workflow.


Choose TaxGPT if your bottleneck extends beyond the return itself. Firms that want standalone citation-backed research, multi-jurisdiction analysis, professional tax drafting, Client Intelligence, return preparation and review, tax planning, and agentic workflows across other areas of the firm can consolidate more of that work into one environment.


For multi-state research, TaxGPT Matrix lets you compare jurisdictions side by side with cited answers. Filed says multi-state return preparation remains in active development.


And if tax memos, IRS notice responses, engagement letters, or other professional drafting consume meaningful hours, TaxGPT offers a dedicated Writer product rather than treating drafting primarily as a supporting function inside prep or planning.


The best test is actual work. When evaluating the platforms, use the same real-world scenarios: a completed return for review, a complex research question, and an IRS notice or professional drafting task. The difference in scope becomes much clearer once the work extends beyond return preparation.


## FAQ


### Q: Does Filed do tax research?


Filed includes tax research within its planning workflow. Tax Planner uses specialist research agents to support strategy recommendations, and its Tax Planning Assistant can answer client-specific questions based on the return and source documents currently under review. However, Filed's research remains tied primarily to its planning workflow. TaxGPT Research is purpose-built for open-ended tax research across federal, state, Canadian, and cross-border issues.


### Q: What’s the difference between TaxGPT and Filed?


Filed is a returns-pipeline platform organized around prep, review, and planning tied to a completed return. TaxGPT is an AI Operating System that also covers research before the return, drafting and client communication around it, and multi-state and Canadian work today.


### Q: Does Filed work in Canada?


No, Filed doesn’t cover Canada. TaxGPT supports the Income Tax Act, CRA guidance, and provincial tax law for firms working on either side of the border.
